'''Ji-Seon Kim''' is a South Korean physicist. She is a Professor in the Department of Physics and Centre for Plastic Electronics at [[Imperial College London]].

== Early life and education ==
Kim grew up in South Korea, and received a BSc in physics at [[Ewha Womans University]] in 1992. She completed a theoretical physics MSc under the supervision of Prof. Jeong Weon Wu in 1994 before moving to the UK to work at the [[University of Cambridge]]. Here she joined the growing research group of Professor [[Richard Friend]], earning a PhD entitled ''Polymer Light-Emitting Diodes: Anode Surface Conditioning and Device Performance'' in 2000.<ref>{{Cite thesis|url=https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/36244973?style=html|title=Polymer Light-Emitting Diodes: Anode Surface Conditioning and Device Performance|last=Kim|first=Ji-Seon|publisher=University of Cambridge|year=2000|degree=PhD|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.621783  }}|accessdate=2018-07-20|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180720165836/https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/36244973?style=html|archivedate=2018-07-20|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Whilst at Cambridge Kim secured an [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council|EPSRC]] Advanced Research Fellowship for the [[Optoelectronics]] group and carried out fundamental research into organic semiconducting materials whilst acting as a technical consultant for [[Cambridge Display Technology|Cambridge Display technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gow.epsrc.ac.uk/NGBOViewGrant.aspx?GrantRef=GR%2FS99075%2F01|title=Grants on the web|language=en|access-date=2017-11-17|archive-date=2018-11-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181108110806/http://gow.epsrc.ac.uk/NGBOViewGrant.aspx?GrantRef=GR%2FS99075%2F01|url-status=dead}}</ref> Kim's research is focussed on nanoanalysis of printed electronic materials, establishing novel printing processes and developing new characterisation techniques.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/people/ji-seon.kim|title=Home - Professor Ji-Seon Kim|website=www.imperial.ac.uk|access-date=2017-11-17}}</ref> In 2003, she was part of the team who won the [[Descartes Prize]] of the European Commission for polymer-based light emitting diodes. Kim joined Imperial College London in 2007 as a lecturer in the Solid State group, where her group have identified spectroscopic and scanning probe techniques that can identify the microstructure and change transport mechanisms within organic materials.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.imperial.ac.uk/nanoanalysis-group/research/developing-nanometrology/|title=Developing Nanometrology|website=Imperial College London|language=en-GB|access-date=2017-11-17}}</ref>  She is a specialist in Resonant [[Raman spectroscopy|Raman Spectroscopy]].

Today she is a Professor of Solid State physics at Imperial College London and a Visiting Professors in Materials Science and Engineering at [[KAIST]], South Korea. She is the director of EPSRC Centre for Doctoral Training in Plastic Electronic Materials at Imperial College London.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.imperial.ac.uk/plastic-electronics/about-us/management-and-advisory-board/|title=Management and Advisory Board {{!}} Research groups {{!}} Imperial College London|website=www.imperial.ac.uk|language=en-GB|access-date=2017-11-17}}</ref> Kim has been involved in strengthening UK-Korea ties, creating strategic partnerships with [[KAIST]] and [[Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology|GIST]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www3.imperial.ac.uk/newsandeventspggrp/imperialcollege/newssummary/news_6-11-2013-10-31-52|title=UK and Korea sign agreement today to advance fuel cell technology|website=Imperial College London|date=6 November 2013 |access-date=2017-11-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www3.imperial.ac.uk/newsandeventspggrp/imperialcollege/newssummary/news_5-11-2013-16-18-47|title=Korean President hails UK science at Imperial|work=Imperial College London|access-date=2017-11-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www3.imperial.ac.uk/newsandeventspggrp/imperialcollege/newssummary/news_9-6-2014-9-43-42|title=Imperial strengthens Korean ties|work=Imperial College London|access-date=2017-11-17}}</ref> In 2016 she signed a memorandum of understanding, creating the GIST-ICL research and development centre.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://ewww.gist.ac.kr/en/html/sub06/060202.html?mode=V&no=145999|title=RISE Holds Joint International Symposium on Plastic Electronics > GIST Excellence|last=GIST|access-date=2017-11-18|language=ko}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.imperial.ac.uk/plastic-electronics/research/collaborations-with-other-research-centres/ic-gist-international-centre/|title=IC-GIST International R&D Centre in Plastic Electronics|website=Imperial College London|language=en-GB|access-date=2017-11-18}}</ref>
